name: Fluid Power
description: Hydraulic and pneumatic circuits drawn to ISO 1219: pumps, valves and cylinders built from parameters, ISO 9461 or ISO 5599 port labels, working, pilot and drain lines, ISO 1219-2 component codes, the displacement-step chart (VDI 3260) and the circuit checks. ISO 1219 (2012) by default, with the 1995 circuit rules and ANSI Y32.10 one choice away.

elementTypes.label: Fluid Power Component
elementTypes.description: Any hydraulic or pneumatic component: it carries the ISO 1219-2 code parts and the data the component list shows.

properties.label: Circuit
properties.description: The circuit number of ISO 1219-2 codes; 0 is the power unit.

properties.label: Installation
properties.description: The installation number written in front of the code, when a plant has several.

properties.label: Code Letter
properties.description: The ISO 1219-2 component letter (P pump or source, A actuator, M prime mover, V valve, S sensor, Z other).

properties.label: Description
properties.description: What the component is, for the component list.

properties.label: Plugged Ports
properties.description: Ports closed with a plug, separated by spaces; an open port listed here is not reported.

elementTypes.label: Source
elementTypes.description: Pumps, compressors and pressure sources.

elementTypes.label: Actuator
elementTypes.description: Cylinders and motors.

elementTypes.label: Prime Mover
elementTypes.description: Electric motors and engines driving a pump.

elementTypes.label: Directional Valve
elementTypes.description: Valves that switch the flow between ports.

properties.label: Paths
properties.description: Flow per position, `;` between positions: `P-A B-T; X; P-B A-T`.

properties.label: Return
properties.description: What brings it back to rest.

properties.label: Rest Position
properties.description: Index of the rest position from the left (0, 1 or 2).

elementTypes.label: Pressure Valve
elementTypes.description: Relief, reducing and sequence valves.

elementTypes.label: Flow Valve
elementTypes.description: Check, throttle, flow control and shut-off valves.

elementTypes.label: Sensor
elementTypes.description: Limit valves and switches, gauges, signal valves.

elementTypes.label: Conditioning
elementTypes.description: Filters, coolers, service units, silencers and exhausts.

elementTypes.label: Tank
elementTypes.description: Reservoirs.

elementTypes.label: Storage
elementTypes.description: Accumulators.

elementTypes.label: Hydraulic Cylinder

properties.label: Pilot

properties.label: Pilot

elementTypes.label: Accumulator

elementTypes.label: Compressor

properties.label: Variable Displacement

elementTypes.label: Air Motor
elementTypes.description: A pneumatic motor turning a shaft.

elementTypes.label: Pneumatic Cylinder

properties.label: Acting

properties.label: Rod
properties.description: A rod at one end or through both.

elementTypes.label: Pressure Switch

elementTypes.label: Limit Switch

elementTypes.label: Electric Motor

elementTypes.label: Enclosure

relationshipTypes.label: Working Line
relationshipTypes.description: A pressure, return or supply line.

relationshipTypes.label: Pilot Line
relationshipTypes.description: A control line to a pilot port.

relationshipTypes.label: Drain Line
relationshipTypes.description: A leakage line to the tank.

relationshipTypes.label: Mechanical Link
relationshipTypes.description: A shaft or a linkage: a motor driving a pump, a rod working a roller.

relationshipTypes.label: Signal Line
relationshipTypes.description: An electrical signal between a sensor and a valve operator.

rules.description: A line joins components it cannot join (a pilot line to a cylinder, a drain line to a pump).
A component that does not belong on this kind of circuit.
Every component code is used once.
Every port is connected or plugged.
Every actuator is driven from a pump, compressor or pressure source.
A fixed displacement pump needs a relief valve on its pressure line.
A hydraulic pump draws from a reservoir.
Port labels follow the medium's port set.
Pilot and drain lines end on pilot and drain ports.
Component codes read as installation, circuit, letter and number.
Each step of the displacement-step chart can be driven by a valve position.
Each step of the displacement-step chart moves an actuator.

rulesets.label: ISO 1219 circuit
rulesets.description: The circuit rules of ISO 1219-2: lines, ports, codes, valves at rest.

rulesets.label: Hydraulic supply
rulesets.description: A relief valve after every fixed pump and a reservoir under every pump.

rulesets.label: Pneumatic ports
rulesets.description: Pneumatic valves numbered by ISO 5599 (also in the circuit rules, so a pneumatic page held only to this set still checks it).

rulesets.label: Displacement-step chart
rulesets.description: Every step drivable and moving an actuator.

examples.label: Hydraulic Circuit with a Cylinder
examples.description: A reservoir, a fixed pump driven by an electric motor, a relief valve with a gauge, a return filter, a 4/3 solenoid valve and a double-acting cylinder, coded 0Z1, 0P1, 0M1, 0V1, 1V1 and 1A1.

examples.label: Pneumatic Circuit with a Sequence
examples.description: A pressure source and service unit, a 5/2 double pilot valve driving a cylinder, two roller limit valves and a start button, with the displacement-step chart beside the circuit.

examples.label: Hydraulic Power Unit
examples.description: A hydraulic power unit in its enclosure: reservoir, fixed pump and motor, relief valve, gauge, cooler and return filter, made by fluid.powerUnit.

variants.label: ISO 1219 (2012)
variants.description: ISO 1219-1 and 1219-2:2012: pilot and drain lines dashed alike; numeric codes by default.

variants.label: ISO 1219 (1995 circuit rules)
variants.description: ISO 1219-2:1995: long dashes for pilot lines, short ones for drains; letter codes such as 1V1.

variants.label: ANSI Y32.10 (US, legacy)
variants.description: ANSI Y32.10 follows the same rules (a symbol shows function, not construction), so the symbols are the same; letter codes. A project that picks JIC symbols draws this (no public JIC fluid power set exists).
